body:
To use the Highlight widget when displaying the search for values results, I need to cheat a little to mimic the regular hits structure. Do you think it's fine to do that here, or should we:
- have the same structure between hits and facetValues in the helper regarding the highlighting
- have several implementations of the higlight in react-instantsearch
This is the name where we need to iterate maybe, items are already facet values. We need to emphasis on the fact that those are search results of facet values right?
Should we also forward the facet search query?
Ideally, it could be nice to be able to get search results for facet values from the searchResults object of the helper. Is that feasible? cc @bobylito
maybe by just adding everytime the prefix `search`, WDYT?

foundFacetValues
searchedFacetValues
facetValuesFromSeach
searchFacetValues (can be tricky, could be a function!)
itemsFromSearch
I like searchedFacetValues but maybe itemsFromSearch is closer than what we already have.

Tricky one! I feel it would be better to have one that is distinct. But as you did it works and it is compatible with the current hits so it make more intuitive to use when building a custom version of this widget. Keep it like that it's great!

One thing we could do for that is merging the `searchResults` object with the searchForFacetValuesResults` as soon as we get one or the other. 

One thing that bothers me though is that the `searchResults` object comes directly from the helper and in our documentation we are actually pointing to the helper documentation to explain its structure. Merging `searchResults` and `searchForFacetValuesResults` wouldn't be a little bit confusing? Can you see another ways?
@vvo I'm not sure to get the question :D you propose to merge the results of the search for facet values (`resultsFacetValues`) into the results object (`results`)?
The results of search for facet values is a "search" which means that the order defined is computed by the engine, as it would for a normal search. Therefore I wouldn't sort them again.
Sorting here doesn't feel right. As discussed, there's no need to place the 'isRefined' items first in case of a SFFV. I'll remove that :)
Yep! The goal being to have a single object as for reading the search results, be it hits, facet values or facet values search results
